A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Sections 1–7, Appendices A–K, all 21 numbered tables, and all 12 figures are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original membership inference, dataset inference, and training-image extraction experiments, together with appendix ablations, comparisons, and mitigation results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the attack evaluations in Tables 1–4 and the supplementary experiments in the appendices.

M1.justification: The conditional-output MIA, MAR adaptations, normalized-sum DI procedure, extraction pipeline, and output-noising defense are unchanged. The expanded Unified MIA discussion describes the Loss Attack already present in v2 Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ImageNet-1k class-conditional setting and the captioned ImageNet-1k VAR-CLIP setting in Appendix B.1. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including the LLM-derived MIAs, DM attacks such as CLiD, DI baseline, and unified Loss Attack. Newly added citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain 10,000 members and 10,000 non-members for MIA/DI, the same model configurations and metrics, and the same extraction settings: 5,000 candidates, SSCD threshold 0.75, and model-specific prefixes in Table 21. Appendix evaluation protocols also match.

E4.justification: The correlation analysis, unified-attack control, MAR ablations, mitigation experiments, prefix-length analysis, and candidate-filtering analysis are retained. Their expanded treatment in Sections 5.1–5.2 summarizes evidence already present in v2 rather than adding analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix H states randomization over 100 experiments in both versions, with unchanged uncertainty reporting in the result tables. DI retains Welch's t-test and the 0.01 threshold; no additional seed or statistical-estimation information is introduced.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted findings match. Both report VAR-d30 MIA TPR@FPR=1% of 86.38%, DI requiring six samples, and extraction of 698 VAR-d30, 36 RAR-XXL, and five MAR-H images. Appendix results and qualitative examples are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss equations, attack formulas, and DI assumptions are unchanged. Converting the notation paragraph into a table adds no mathematical content, and neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The four central contributions and claims about privacy, utility, and efficiency retain their scope. v4 omits the abstract's diffusion-based mitigation suggestion, but retains that prospect in Section 6 and the same substantive conclusions.

C2.justification: The expanded main-text explanations restate existing arguments about architectural leakage, model size, training duration, and MIA signals underlying DI. Appendix B's applicability and comparison limitations, memorization interpretations, and qualifications about the heuristic defense remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The model details, attack hyperparameters, hardware, cost-estimation procedures, and sampling instructions are retained. Both provide the same code repository; v4's revised release wording does not document a change in access or availability.

R1.justification: v4 adds references on LLM privacy, memorization, and dataset inference, including Hayes et al. (2025), Hintersdorf et al. (2024), and Zhao et al. (2025). These broaden citation coverage without substantially changing research positioning. CDI's publication update is not a new work.

P1.justification: v4 adds introductory signposting and expands explanatory paragraphs in Sections 5.1–5.2. It also shortens the abstract and updates headings, affiliations, and acknowledgments. Most prose and the ordering of sections and appendices remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column format to a two-column conference layout, with new running headers and widespread resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. Section 2 gains a notation table replacing prose. Existing scientific displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the existing architectural, correlation, and unified-attack arguments easier to find through expanded explanations in Sections 5.1–5.2, and the notation table improves reference use. These provide a limited gain in accessibility. The empirical evidence and substantive limitations in Appendix B remain unchanged.
